description: No mark or detail on the garment beyond the interior label; photos show plain linen pieces.
note: Checked on 120percento.com: Regular Fit Shirt with Pockets, Slim Fit Linen Shirt, Hooded T-Shirt. Photos at small scale show plain garments, no external mark. Brand story page had no mention of a signature mark.

description: The brand's own camouflage print, sold under the name ABC Camo, used all-over on jackets, hoodies and accessories.
note: Also: the Ape Head logo (product title Multi Ape Head Tee on us.bape.com). Brand product pages name ABC Camo as a pattern, but the sample I opened was the BAPE x SUBU camo puffer sandals, not a garment body; the camo-on-garment placement was not seen. No heritage page or press read; a newsletter pop-up covered each page and was not touched. Needs a garment example and a press source.

description: The brand name in its own wide block capitals, printed across the front of the Axel tote.
placement: front of bag (garment placement not seen)
note: Ruled a yes by Sebastian: the block-letter wordmark is the tell. Seen on the brand product photo of the Axel small tote (letters across the front). The garments I opened earlier (Dylan sweater, Luis duffle, Auster mac) showed no large mark, only a small one at the mac chest, so garment placement is unconfirmed. No brand history page or press read.

description: No mark seen on current product; the moose icon is the historic mark but was not seen on the pieces checked.
note: Checked on abercrombie.com: Essential Ultra Baggy Open Hem Sweatpant, Essential Half-Zip Sweatshirt, 100% Merino Wool 3-Button Collared Sweater. Photos show no external mark on any. The moose icon is a known past mark but no current garment I opened carried it, so I cannot call it a current tell or none. Sign-in and cookie panels were left alone.

description: A small embroidered or printed face of two dots and a straight line, used as a patch or print across knitwear, accessories and sweatshirts.
note: Face line. Per Sebastian the Face counts as the tell. Brand product page: knit beanie with a large embroidered Face logo patch. Highsnobiety calls it a recognised motif drawn by Jonny Johansson, no year. Placement varies, so no single spot; the beanie sample is not a garment body. The brand About page had no text on the Face. Also: the Canada scarf (signature product, not checked).

description: Three parallel stripes running along the side of the shoe, and down the sleeves or legs on clothing.
placement: shoe side; sleeves and legs on clothing
note: adidas Group history page: in 1949 Adi Dassler registered a shoe featuring the 3-Stripes. Samba OG product photo shows the three stripes on the shoe side. Clothing placement (sleeves, legs) is not from a page I read this pass. Also: the Trefoil (not checked).

description: No mark seen on the garment I opened; the jacket shows plain quilting and snaps.
note: Checked on aetherapparel.com: Stella Liner Jacket (orange) and the Bamford D-300 watch collab; the homepage exposed only eight product links, so only one garment was read. Photos show no external mark on the jacket. Signature Mulholland jacket not opened. Needs more garments.

description: No mark seen on the front and side photos of the jeans opened.
note: Checked on agjeans.com: Brinley Jean (mid-rise straight) and Billie Jean (relaxed straight), front and side photos at small scale. Back-pocket photos were not examined, which is where a jean mark would be, so this is low. Tellis jean not opened.

description: No mark seen on the garments opened; the pieces are plain.
note: Checked on agolde.com: Shara Pant (satin cargo) and Napier Shirt (satin stripe); a newsletter pop-up covered part of the second page and was not touched. No jeans were opened, and the 90s straight jean (the signature product) is where a back-pocket mark would show, so this is low.

description: A stylised MA monogram, shown as a signature MA lapel pin on the sport blazer and used as a mark on other pieces.
note: Brand product text on the Single Breasted Sport Blazer: finished with a signature MA lapel pin. One product read; the MX1 jean (signature product) and any bandana print were not opened, so the most recognised mark may be a different one. No press read.

description: No mark or detail on the garment beyond the interior labels; product photos show plain garments.
note: Checked on asket.com: Merino Sweater (dark navy), Heavy Wool Sweater (charcoal melange), Recycled Cashmere Sweater (dark grey), and The T-Shirt (white, women's page). Photos and detail lists show no external mark; product pages list only main label and care label. Details named are minimal fully fashioned finishes and twin-needle stitching, which are construction, not a brand mark. Cookie banner left untouched; screenshots were partly dimmed by it.

description: A Fraser Tartan cotton lining inside the G9 Harrington jacket, with a ribbed dog-ear collar.
note: Brand product text for the G9 Ltd 3rd Edition lists Fraser Tartan lining in 100% cotton and a ribbed dog-ear collar; the page says the G9 debuted in 1937 (that dates the jacket, not the tartan). A newsletter pop-up covered the page and was not touched, so I could not see the lining in the photo. One brand source only. Also: the dog-ear collar.

description: A Classic Tartan lining inside the waxed jacket, with a contrast cord collar; the tartan shows at the cuffs and collar.
note: Brand product text on the Icons Beaufort: contrast colour cord collar, and a panelled Classic Tartan lining delivering signature Barbour heritage styling. Product photo shows tartan at the cuff. The Bedale itself was not opened; the Beaufort carries the same features. The second link is a brand tartan page I did not open, only saw in the nav. Also: the corduroy collar on the Bedale (per the worklist, not checked).

description: A camel, black, red and white check, woven as the lining of the heritage trench coat and used on other pieces.
note: Brand product page has a section called The Check: an enduring house code, the iconic check lining woven at the Burberry Mill in Yorkshire. Listing photos show the check at the collar lining. Wikipedia: in use since at least the 1920s, mainly as trench lining. Also: the Equestrian Knight mark (not checked).

description: A round logo disc patch on the upper sleeve of the parka.
note: Product photo of the Snow Mantra Parka shows the round disc patch on the upper arm (the photo side is the wearer right here, so I give no left or right). The site names a Black Disc variant of the Langford parka in the related-product text, which supports the disc as the brand's patch. No heritage page or press read; the Expedition parka (signature product) was not opened. Also: the sleeve patch is also called the Arctic Program patch (name not confirmed on a page I read, so the tell name is provisional).

description: A small red cloth label with white LEVI'S lettering sewn into the seam of the right back pocket.
note: Levi Strauss corporate page gives 1 Sept 1936 and the right back pocket of the 501. On the 501 product page the side-view photo shows a small tab at the back pocket (zoomed, small). Denim Hunters link was from search results and was not opened this pass.

description: A blank label held by four visible stitches at the back of the garment.
note: Brand product spec on the denim jacket reads: Four stitches at the back. The page says back, not back neck; the neck position is not confirmed on the product page. No brand heritage page naming the stitches was found in the pass. Even Magazine (not on the approved list) says the stitches show on a blank white label; no year stated.

description: A round patch with the Moncler cockerel logo on the upper sleeve of the down jacket.
note: Placement seen on the Maya 70 product photo: round patch on the upper sleeve (zoomed; small). Brand history page: the cockerel permanently replaced the earlier logo in 1968; that dates the logo, not necessarily the sleeve patch. The page does not say felt; Wikipedia lists a felt appliqué badge among core elements. Product text had no mention of the patch.

description: A small embroidered polo player on horseback, on the left chest of the polo shirt.
note: Brand article: the pony first used in 1971 on a women's shirt cuff; Polo shirt followed in 1972; 1,100 stitches. Left-chest placement seen on the Iconic Mesh Polo product photo. The Complex link came from search and was not opened this pass.

description: A removable cloth badge with a compass-rose insignia, buttoned to the upper left sleeve of the jacket.
note: About page: badge created in 1982 on the first Tela Stella jacket. Sleeve placement seen on the 41NS001 hooded jacket photo (badge on the wearer left sleeve). Wikipedia: edging green until about 2000, then black. Button-on detail is from Wikipedia, not the brand page.

description: A signature red, white and blue striped grosgrain loop tab at the back of the neck, with the same stripe as trim on side vents and cuffs.
placement: back neck; also trim and armbands
note: Brand product text on the 4-Bar polo: signature striped grosgrain loop tab at back of neck, and signature striped grosgrain trim on side vents. Colours red, white and blue come from the brand logo stripe on the site header and the brief, not the product text. Also: the 4-bar stripe on the left sleeve (stated on the same page). Wikipedia says every piece carries the ribbon, citing The New Yorker, 18 Sep 2023 (not opened). No start year stated.

description: No mark or detail on the garment beyond the printed name; product photos show plain garments.
note: Checked on uniqlo.com/us: Unisex Sweat Half-Zip Pullover, Unisex Flannel Shirt (heather), Men's Cashmere Sweater, Unisex Sweat Oversized Pullover Hoodie. A sign-up pop-up (phone number, $5 off) sat over each page; I did not enter anything or accept it, and read the product photos behind it.
